1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nf3 Bg7 4.g3 d6 5.Bg2.strategy: Castles and completes the set-up in which both kings sit behind fianchettoed bishops. White's kingside is more solid than in most King's Indian lines, so Black's usual attack on the king hardly works, and the fight is for the centre and c4.

Pressures d4 and prepares to challenge the centre, and the knight can later head for the edge to bear down on c4, the weak point of the fianchetto set-up. Black trades a little comfort for lasting queenside pressure; White must keep c4 covered.

Supports the e5 advance with a piece and leaves the c-pawn and the c8-bishop untouched. Black aims to claim the centre with ...e5, the plan of the classical King's Indian, and White has to decide how to meet it.

Hits d4 with the c-pawn instead of the e-pawn, trading a wing pawn for a central one and moving Black's counterplay to the queenside. White decides whether to release the tension or to gain space; if the centre opens, the g7 bishop gains scope.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nf3 Bg7 4.g3 d6 5.Bg2.name: King's Indian Defence: Fianchetto Variation, Yugoslav System

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nf3 Bg7 4.g3 d6 5.Bg2.strategy: A restrained pawn move that supports a later ...d5 and gives the queen the b6 and a5 squares. Black claims no space yet, so White can take time to build a position.
